clue.text: Top Gear star appearing with famous interviewer and footballer

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star
Sir Robin Day was a famously combative British TV political interviewer
George Best was a celebrated Northern Irish footballer

explanation.surface: A presenter from the TV motoring show Top Gear turns up alongside a well-known interviewer and a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Gear' looks like the BBC motoring programme, but it means one's finest clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Your finest clothing, kept for church and special occasions, is top-notch attire, or top gear.

clue.text: Sort of condition that's set in stone

indicators.note: something set in a frame sits inside it, so the condition goes inside the stone

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A sort of condition that is set in stone, i.e. a fixed rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To sift things is to sort them, separating one kind from another as with a sieve.

clue.text: Thinnest bolt has to fit inside casing

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, the casing around the bolt

parts.note: a nest is a snug enclosure, as with a nest of tables fitting one inside another
a bolt is a short arrow shot from a crossbow

explanation.surface: Instructions for a mechanic: the slimmest bolt must fit inside its housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowest and thinnest are superlative synonyms, both meaning having the least width.

clue.text: Hairdo often too elaborate for a start?

indicators.note: an elaborate version is worked up and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hairdo far too elaborate to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HAIRDO OFTEN TOO are rearranged. The definition is playful: getting a foot in the door gives you a start.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an initial opening or entry from which further progress can be made.

clue.text: Book is one that's got abridged about one of the Bourbons?

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, so the shortened word surrounds the numeral

parts.note: an abridged text has been cut
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A book about one of the French royal Bourbons, cut down in length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bourbons' suggests the French royal house, but a Bourbon is a British chocolate biscuit. The setter uses 'one' twice, once in the wordplay and again in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bourbon is a well-known British chocolate-cream sandwich cookie, so it is one example of this treat.

clue.text: He's no longer happy if forgetting name?

definitions.text: He's no longer happy if forgetting name?

parts.words: He's no longer happy if forgetting name?
parts.note: the figure in a British saying about being very cheerful; drop N (name) from his title and what remains reads SAD BOY, someone no longer happy

explanation.surface: Someone loses their cheer on forgetting a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy as a sandboy' is a British saying meaning very cheerful. Remove N for name and the word becomes SAD BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbially cheerful figure of the British saying turns into a sad lad once the N is gone.

clue.text: Pleased with oneself, having succeeded with attack

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
to mug is to attack and rob someone

explanation.surface: A mugger feels self-satisfied after a successful assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes complacent self-satisfaction, being too pleased with yourself.

clue.text: Oil press for two

definitions.meaning: oil paint is an artist's medium; 'for two' asks for the plural, two such mediums
the press means newspapers and broadcasters, the news outlets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil press' looks like a machine for crushing olives. 'for two' turns the first sense plural: two mediums, such as oil and watercolour.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of medium covers artistic materials like oil, while the press is the journalistic sense.

clue.text: Guzzler sounding high after opening gallon bottle

indicators.note: the shrill word comes after the gallon's first letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a reedy voice sounds thin and high-pitched
bottle is British slang for courage, as is guts

explanation.surface: A drinker gulps down a gallon bottle, making a high-pitched sound after opening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container, but here it is British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy-guts is a colloquial term for a glutton who eats or drinks too much.

clue.text: Input device in question intricately worked by tray close to cable

indicators.note: worked intricately suggests letters woven into a new pattern
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A computer peripheral is being described as made from a tray and some cable.
explanation.walkthrough: Q is followed by the rearranged letters of WORKED BY TRAY plus E, the final letter of 'cable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard typing keyboard, named for its first six letter keys, is a means of entering data.

clue.text: What Green is making sacrifice?

definitions.meaning: at a traffic light, green means proceed: split the answer into a three-letter preposition and that two-letter verb
to sacrifice something is to give it up or do without it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like an environmentalist making sacrifices, but it is the traffic-light colour, which stands for 'proceed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to give up or do without something, voluntarily surrendering it.

clue.text: Club Polish joined, say, after coming west

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed after the others

parts.note: to sand wood is to polish it smooth
wed means joined in marriage

indicators.note: in an across answer, westward travel is right to left, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Someone joins a polishing firm, say, after heading out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' could be the nationality, but it is the verb. The golf sense of 'Club' is hidden by the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This lofted iron is a golf club used for playing out of bunkers.

clue.text: Boy turned hitch-hiker to get where he wants to go?

indicators.note: turned round means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name
a hitch-hiker thumbs lifts, so is a thumber
to land a job is to get it

explanation.surface: A lad becomes a hitch-hiker to reach his destination.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the hitch-hiker's destination; NORTHUMBERLAND is a county in the far north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A county is a destination a traveller may be heading for, with the question mark flagging the example.

clue.text: Bird, when on corner, to gesture defiantly

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a nook is a corner or recess

explanation.surface: A rooster in a corner makes a defiant gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock a snook is to thumb the nose at someone, a mocking sign of contempt.

clue.text: Fish wrongly done after having bits taken off?

parts.note: when something is over it is done, finished
net describes what remains after deductions, as net pay after tax

explanation.surface: A fish was badly cooked after being trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a noun on a plate, but it is a verb: to overnet is to deplete waters by fishing too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnetting is excessive fishing with nets, harvesting more than stocks can bear.

clue.text: Fluctuating that involves one in endless meditation?

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
without its end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: yoga is a meditative practice

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the numeral goes within the word for that

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wavering between moods, like someone caught in unending meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' as yon is archaic or Scots, a convention worth knowing. 'involves' wraps it round I, giving YOIN; 'in' sets that inside YOG, the meditation cut short by 'endless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Going up and down like the toy on a string means varying or wavering repeatedly.

clue.text: Drive up motorway, turning left before hill

indicators.note: the letter for left comes before the hill
turning around means these letters are read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, from London to Leeds
Sion, or Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: Directions for driving up the motorway, turning left before a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a motoring verb but is the noun meaning urge. 'turning' reverses UP plus MI, giving IMPU.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulsion is an impelling force or urge, the same as an inner drive.

clue.text: Sauce boat lifted

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
lifted means raised, up

explanation.surface: A gravy boat raised at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' suggests a gravy jug, but 'boat' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato condiment is a sauce, spread on chips and burgers.

clue.text: A tip: dry ground is something worth digging

indicators.note: ground up means broken down and reformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: parched earth is worth digging over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground rich in gold or ore repays the miner's labour, hence a lucrative find worth excavating.

clue.text: Mark of some relevance? Yes, potentially

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a mark has any relevance and is told it might.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyespot is a round marking resembling an eye, as on a butterfly's wing.

clue.text: French in luck after missing initial boost

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: after losing its first letter, the word is trimmed at the front

parts.note: chance means luck

explanation.surface: A French gambler gets a boost from a lucky break once the first hurdle is missed.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to improve or raise it, giving it a lift.

clue.text: Receiving delivery when someone rings before ten

definitions.text: Receiving delivery when someone rings before ten

parts.words: Receiving delivery when someone rings before ten
parts.note: in boxing, a floored fighter is rescued if the bell ending the round sounds before the count of ten; delivery means rescue

explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' and 'rings' suggest a parcel at the door, but delivery is rescue and the bell is the boxing bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means rescued at the last moment, from a boxer spared by the end-of-round signal.

clue.text: Jumper may have this very small victory margin

parts.note: in horse racing, winning by a neck is a narrow margin

explanation.surface: A showjumper wins by a tiny margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a horse, fitting the racing margin, but it is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater can be cut with a pointed collar shape, so the style is a feature it may have.

clue.text: Got nicked regularly, but no more?

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter

explanation.surface: A reformed thief got caught regularly, but not any longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some past time, describing something that happens no longer.

clue.text: Ignore an old, decrepit, statesman

indicators.note: decrepit means broken down, so these letters fall apart and reform

explanation.surface: Advice to overlook an aged, frail politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' looks like a politician but means a man from a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Oregon is literally a man of that American state, a playful reading of statesman.

clue.text: Article that's seized by bird

definitions.note: the answer is chiefly an adjective but is also used as a noun for a bird

indicators.note: the article grips the other word inside it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
via means by way of

explanation.surface: An item grabbed by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word denotes a bird, any feathered creature in the class Aves.

clue.text: He had a list put out twice

indicators.note: twice means the piece is written two times in a row

parts.note: KO is a knockout, putting a boxer out

explanation.surface: Someone had a list of jobs put out twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, the Lord High Executioner sings 'I've got a little list'.
explanation.definitionFit: The executioner in The Mikado keeps a little list of people who would not be missed.

clue.text: People there groomed and neat, etc

indicators.note: groomed means tidied and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Guests at an event, all well groomed and neat and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnout at an event is the number of people present, those who came.
